headline: Utah GOP governor on Trump and 2028: ‘It’s time for the next thing’
author: Lauren Fedor

paragraphs.text: Utah’s Republican governor wants his party to move beyond President Donald Trump heading into the next presidential election.

“It’s time for the next thing,” Gov. Spencer Cox said in an interview on Wednesday at the POLITICO Pub, on the sidelines of the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum in Deer Valley, Utah.
Cox called on his fellow Republicans to start looking for new leadership in the wake of this month’s midterm election defeats.
“This is how this works when presidents move on. We should be looking for the next leadership in our party and what that looks like,” Cox told POLITICO’s Samuel Benson.

“We’ve got JD Vance and Marco Rubio, and those seem to be kind of the two choices now,” Cox said, referring to the Vice President and Secretary of State, respectively. “But I think you’ll see a lot of people step up … there are a lot of really interesting folks.”
“I’m a fan of governors,” Cox added. “I think governors with executive experience are the best to lead the country.”

Vance told Fox News earlier this week that he would decide “sometime next year” whether he will run for president in 2028. Rubio has dismissed suggestions that he would launch his own bid, and has said he would support Vance if the Vice President ran for the White House.
“I am hopeful that there are some Republican governors that will throw their hat in,” said Cox, a two-term governor. “We can have a competition of ideas heading in to find out what's next.”

Cox said that Trump still has a “really important role to play” in leading the party over the next two years, adding that the president still had an “opportunity” to strike bipartisan deals on permitting reform and other policy areas in his last two years in office.
Cox called the president “unique,” adding: “He’s someone who has the attention of the country in a way that almost no president has had in my lifetime.”
“People really love him or really don’t like him, but everybody’s paying attention to him,” he said.
